title: The CPU Builder
briefing: Head office wants custom CPUs: 4 cores, 8 cores, 16 cores, whatever the customer orders. Writing the same code for every order is madness. Build reusable functions instead: little machines you set up once and use forever. Other floors will call your functions later, so make them solid!
hints: A function starts with def name(parameters): and uses return to hand back a result. A default value looks like clock_ghz=3.0 in the brackets.

is_faulty should return True when the clock is 0 OR the temperature is over 100. You can return a comparison directly: return a or b. *cpus collects any number of arguments into a tuple you can loop over.

def build_cpu(cores, clock_ghz=3.0): return {"cores": cores, "clock_ghz": clock_ghz, "score": cores * clock_ghz} / def is_faulty(cpu): return cpu["clock_ghz"] == 0 or cpu["temp_c"] > 100 / def total_cores(*cpus): total = 0, then for cpu in cpus: total += cpu["cores"], then return total
bonus: Write describe(cpu) that returns a sentence like '8-core CPU at 4.0 GHz'. Call it using keyword arguments, e.g. build_cpu(clock_ghz=5.0, cores=6).
